about: Goals and tentpoles for the dashboard's front page and Goals page.

progress says how the bar is computed, never guessed: steps (share of steps done; a step with a pr is done when that PR is merged on GitHub, a step with hill is done when the newest measured point meets atMost or atLeast, any other step needs done and evidence), device (the first and newest measured points of a devices.json line against its goal point), hill (the first and newest measured points of a hillclimb.json series against target), or upstream (PRs merged on Max's game out of every PR offered there, open and closed ones included, live from GitHub).
full says what 100% means. match is a regex on PR titles that ties PRs to the goal; a step's pr counts too. waiting names open PRs held for a check, shown as their status.

goals.name: CPU, power and smoothness
goals.plain: Cut what my game spends on each draw, so a core gets idle time every frame and fans stay quiet.
goals.full: All five roadmap phases landed with measured A/B numbers, and the RTX laptop's main thread under 16.7 ms walking through town.

steps.label: Practice host in a worker (phase 2, behind a flag; not turned on: input-to-ack p95 is 10 to 16 ms worse on the RTX laptop)
Draw-list lab: a replayed draw costs 4.79 µs against 15.3 µs in three.js (n=8, RTX laptop)
Relative energy-impact baseline on a Mac (partial: Safari High still to come)
Phase 1: per-draw fixes bring the RTX main thread under 16.7 ms
Phase 4: per-pass GPU timers and budgets per tier
Phase 5: battery and thermal mode (my call, with A/B numbers)

goals.name: Checks that stop regressions
goals.plain: Every PR is checked so memory, speed, loading and looks can't quietly get worse.
goals.full: Every PR checked for memory, performance, load time and visuals, with a comment showing what changed.

Memory in a match and in low-memory mode

goals.plain: Fit a whole match on 16 GB Macs in Safari, then 12 GB and 10 GB machines.
goals.full: Safari's whole-browser peak in a match at the plan's 3,850 MB target on a 16 GB Mac.

steps.label: Free far-away places in low-memory mode
Safari finishes a match on a 16 GB Mac

goals.plain: Safari at High on a Retina Mac should hold 60 fps, not snap to 30.
goals.full: 60 fps at High, DPR 2, in Safari on the Mac.

goals.plain: WebTransport so a lost packet doesn't hold up every input behind it.
goals.full: Tested with real players against WebSockets, and switched on by default if it wins.

Decide the default from the numbers

goals.full: Matches spread across cores, benchmarked with 50 players per match.

goals.plain: Esc → REPORT A PROBLEM sends me your logs, a replay and a screenshot, and I sort them into clusters.
goals.full: Players can send a report in one click, and every report lands in a ranked queue I can fix from.
